purpose: Turn the internet-lolcow phenomenon into an analytical idea for the Farm/Swamp model rather than a harassment list or a database of private people.
epistemic_rule: A person appearing in this atlas means that public online communities have made them a recurring subject of attention, commentary, archiving or conflict. It does not mean the project endorses harassment, believes every allegation, or considers the person's identity reducible to the label.
measurement_rule: Farm footprint is not a moral score. Where an actual forum page count is available it is recorded as such. Otherwise the repository records article counts, thread counts, messages, or simply 'not measured'. Never invent a page count.
idea: The Farm is better understood as an ecology of attention than as a list of cows. A figure enters when unusual behaviour, controversy, conflict, politics, celebrity, eccentricity, scandal, vulnerability, spectacle or repeated audience interaction creates a self-reinforcing archive. The important object is therefore the relationship between subject, observers, content producers, platforms, archives, audiences, money and time.

figures.name: Chris Chan
figures.public_role: YouTuber, artist and creator of Sonichu
figures.why_attention_accumulated: The Chris Chan phenomenon combined a long-running personal online presence, Sonichu, romantic and social narratives, repeated public conflicts, extensive trolling and an unusually durable archive. The later criminal case radically changed the nature of the story, but did not create the phenomenon itself.
figures.political_or_personality_axis: primarily personality/identity/creative-internet culture rather than originally political
figures.farm_footprint: approximately 2,965 CWCki articles as of 2026-09-08; this is the size of the dedicated encyclopedia, not 2,965 articles all solely about Chris as an individual
figures.audience_role: observers, documentarians, trolls, commentators and archivists
figures.creator_role: Chris's own content generated primary material; later creators generated commentary and documentary material
figures.monetization: mixed; audience attention, creative work, media/documentary interest and platform activity
figures.evidence_notes: CWCki describes itself as the encyclopedia for Chris Chan and currently reports 2,965 articles; it also explicitly warns readers not to contact or seek out people associated with the subject.

figures.name: Cyraxx / Chance Wilkins
figures.why_attention_accumulated: A persistent cycle of public livestreaming, confrontational responses, exaggerated self-presentation, disputes with trolls and other online figures, and repeated attempts to control the narrative around himself produced an unusually large feedback loop.
figures.farm_footprint: over 2,500 pages in the documented Kiwi Farms Cyraxx thread; exact current page count should be re-measured rather than treated as static
figures.audience_role: trolls, observers, archivists, commentators and cross-community audiences
figures.creator_role: Cyraxx produces primary content while commentators and trolls transform reactions into secondary content
figures.monetization: livestream donations and secondary commentary exist as observable economic channels; exact totals require source-level accounting
figures.evidence_notes: The Cyraxx Wiki states the Kiwi Farms thread exceeded 2,500 pages and describes the subject as one of its largest threads.

figures.name: MusicBizMarty / Nicholas Beigler
figures.public_role: YouTuber and livestreamer associated especially with Cyraxx commentary and trolling
figures.why_attention_accumulated: Marty became important because he did not merely observe the Farm; he actively participated in the content-production loop around Cyraxx. The confrontation itself became the product, creating a strong Farmer-to-Cow feedback relationship.
figures.farm_footprint: a dedicated Kiwi Farms thread is documented; current recoverable page count not established in this pass
figures.footprint_measurement_type: dedicated forum thread; page count pending archival measurement
figures.duration_to_2026_09_08: about 6 years of documented activity before death, with posthumous discussion continuing
figures.audience_role: participants, spectators, commentators and archive consumers
figures.creator_role: active Farmer/content producer as well as subject of Farm attention
figures.monetization: livestream/content attention; exact financial flows require separate accounting
figures.death_status: deceased; source records January 29 2025 as death date
figures.evidence_notes: The Cyraxx Wiki describes Marty as a prominent Cyraxx troll and says he died from an overdose on January 29 2025. Death-related claims should be independently verified before being treated as final biographical facts.

figures.name: Daniel Larson
figures.why_attention_accumulated: A rapid growth in online visibility, unusual self-presentation, repeated public incidents, interactions with trolls, homelessness, legal trouble and a large archive of videos created a highly recursive attention cycle.
figures.political_or_personality_axis: primarily personality, spectacle and conflict; politics became one subtheme
figures.farm_footprint: 429 articles on the dedicated Daniel Larson Wiki as of the latest indexed page; the wiki reports 24,449 edits
figures.audience_role: observers, trolls, journalists, archivists and documentary communities
figures.creator_role: primary content creator plus a large secondary archival ecosystem
figures.monetization: platform attention and secondary commentary; exact revenue requires source-level data
figures.evidence_notes: The dedicated wiki currently reports 429 articles and 24,449 edits and maintains an explicit neutrality/evidence policy. It also documents traditional and internet media coverage.

figures.name: KingCobraJFS / Joshua Fay Saunders
figures.why_attention_accumulated: His unusual lifestyle, eccentric crafts, food videos, alcohol-centered streaming and repeated controversies generated sustained fascination. Unlike some figures, the archive also records a genuine audience of fans attracted to the creative eccentricity itself.
figures.farm_footprint: documented as a named historical individual in lolcow archives; a precise aggregate page count was not established in this pass
figures.audience_role: fans, observers, commentators and archive communities
figures.creator_role: primary creator whose own eccentric lifestyle generated the raw material
figures.monetization: YouTube/streaming and merchandise-type creator economy channels; exact lifetime totals require separate research
figures.evidence_notes: The Cyraxx Wiki describes KingCobraJFS as less infamous than some major lolcows while noting that he had legitimate fans. This is analytically useful: Farm attention is not identical to universal hostility.

figures.name: Donald J. Trump
figures.farm_entry_period: long before the modern Farm; intensified during the social-media era
figures.why_attention_accumulated: Trump is a useful boundary case because enormous attention is generated not by a niche lolcow community alone but by mass politics, television, social media, opposition research, supporters, journalists, parody, legal controversy and political campaigning.
figures.farm_footprint: Onion Farms currently lists a Trump Family & Orbiters section with 5 threads and 6 messages, plus a dedicated Donald J Trump thread; this is only a small visible slice of his much larger cross-platform attention footprint and must not be treated as his total Farm footprint
figures.approx_start: pre-social-media political celebrity; Farm-style internet attention especially intensified in the 2010s
figures.audience_role: mass political electorate, supporters, opponents, journalists, creators and meme communities
figures.creator_role: political communicator as well as subject of enormous third-party content production
figures.monetization: political fundraising, media attention, books, merchandise, advertising and creator-economy spillovers exist across the broader ecosystem
figures.evidence_notes: Trump should not simply be called a conventional lolcow. He is better modeled as a boundary case demonstrating how the same attention-extraction mechanics can exist at mass political scale.

figures.name: Tophiachu / Tophia Slydell
figures.why_attention_accumulated: Persistent social-media visibility, public disputes, family-related drama, homelessness/housing discussion and repeated online conflicts have made Tophia a recurring subject in lolcow communities.
figures.farm_footprint: current exact page count not established in this pass; should be measured across dedicated threads and archives rather than guessed
figures.audience_role: commentators, observers, trolls and social-media audiences
figures.monetization: creator-platform attention; exact figures require source-level accounting
figures.evidence_notes: The name appears repeatedly in Cyraxx-related archival material, but this atlas deliberately avoids importing unverified allegations as facts.

figures.name: The Farm itself
figures.why_attention_accumulated: The Farm emerges when eccentricity, controversy, documentation, audience participation, trolling, algorithms, platform monetization and archival persistence reinforce each other.
figures.political_or_personality_axis: not a person; spans personality, politics, celebrity, ideology and internet culture
figures.farm_footprint: A preserved Kiwi Farms snapshot records 147,951 threads and 16,493,021 messages; a current Onion Farms snapshot shows numerous categories and thousands of additional threads. These are ecosystem measurements, not measures of harm.
figures.approx_start: 2000s roots; CWCki/Kiwi Farms lineage becomes especially relevant in the 2009-2010s period
major_cycles: new archival mirrors and successor communities
figures.audience_role: observers, participants, archivists, trolls, creators, journalists and researchers
figures.creator_role: distributed across subjects, commentators and forum users
figures.monetization: forum memberships/donations, creator monetization, advertising, subscriptions, merchandise and indirect attention economics depending on platform
figures.evidence_notes: The system-level record is more important than any individual. It lets the project study how a person becomes a recurring object of attention, how the archive grows, and how the audience can become a producer of new material.

analytical_model.not_a_database: The desired output is an idea of the Farm as a living ecology, with databases serving as measurement instruments rather than the final conceptual object.
analytical_model.cow_entry: unusual behaviour or identity -> public exposure -> audience curiosity -> documentation -> reaction -> secondary content -> conflict -> more exposure
analytical_model.farmer_entry: observer becomes creator -> creator becomes participant -> participant acquires audience -> audience rewards continued harvesting
analytical_model.milk: observable attention output: views, comments, watch time, posts, threads, donations, subscriptions, advertising, political engagement and other measurable flows
analytical_model.mud: negative traces accumulated through allegations, conflicts, legal records, humiliations, corrections, screenshots and reputational events
analytical_model.entanglement: connections among subject, farmer, platform, audience, lawyers, journalists, family, employers, political actors, advertisers and archives
analytical_model.death_state: Death does not necessarily end a Farm. It can transform a live attention cycle into a historical archive, where old material is preserved, remixed and reinterpreted.
analytical_model.key_question: Instead of asking only 'who is a lolcow?', ask 'what process turns a human being into a persistent object of collective attention, and what does every participant gain, lose, produce or accumulate as the process continues?'
